summary: Tested all new auth, protected lead CRUD, admin E2E, Case Studies/logo/favicon, unknown-route fallback, mobile admin layout, seed-update behavior, and production build. Frontend flows pass; backend has two security-control failures: public lockout does not occur after five failures, and credentialed CORS uses a wildcard origin.

critical.issue: Five failed attempts for lockme@test.com do not trigger lockout; the sixth request still returns 401 instead of 429. Public ingress requests alternate between proxy addresses, splitting counters by request.client.host, so the per-IP/email threshold is bypassed.

critical.endpoint: CORS preflight for /api/auth/login and credentialed APIs
critical.issue: Preflight returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true instead of the explicit frontend origin. This violates the required credentialed-CORS configuration and is invalid for cross-origin cookie requests.

action_items: Make login throttling use a stable, trusted client identity behind ingress (or email/account-based throttling) and perform the counter increment/check atomically; verify the sixth request after five failures returns 429.
Configure CORS_ORIGINS as an explicit allowlist containing the deployed frontend origin; reject wildcard configuration when allow_credentials is enabled.
Re-run the backend suite and auth UI smoke test after both security fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py keys login attempts with request.client.host, which is an ingress/proxy address in this environment. Observed seven sequential requests split between 10.79.142.66 and 10.79.142.69, preventing either counter from reaching five.
server.py combines allow_credentials=True with CORS_ORIGINS='*'. Credentialed CORS requires explicit origins; the public preflight currently emits the invalid wildcard/credentials combination.
The lockout read-before-increment sequence is also non-atomic, so concurrent failures can race even after client identity is stabilized.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_ contact leads and a transient test admin record for seed-password update verification; all test contacts, test users, and lockout probe records were deleted (verified zero remain).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Passing backend coverage includes login user/cookie attributes, me, refresh, logout cookie clearing, wrong password, unauthenticated 401s, authenticated contact create/list/delete persistence, unknown delete 404, contact validation regressions, bcrypt $2b$ hash, indexes, and seed_admin updating an existing stale hash. Frontend passing coverage includes wrong/correct login, lead count, refresh, logout, homepage contact-to-inbox-to-delete with toast and persistence check, Work scrolling, all 3 case studies/content/images, nav/footer SVG logos, SVG favicon, mobile admin no overflow, and unknown-route fallback. Production yarn build compiles. One pre-existing non-test lead remains untouched.
rca_of_the_issue: Lockout RCA: the key is constructed as request.client.host + email, but ingress load-balancing exposes changing proxy pod IPs rather than a stable end-user IP; attempts are distributed across records. CORS RCA: backend/.env sets CORS_ORIGINS='*' and server.py passes it directly to CORSMiddleware while enabling credentials. Reproduction: run the final pytest suite; the lockout and explicit-origin CORS cases are the only two failures.
